svg.text: How the AI engine learns optimal hotel rates — architecture, feedback, and validation
9 PRICE ARMS · 20+ CONTEXT SIGNALS · 2-TIER MODEL · NIGHTLY QUALITY GATE
Every pricing decision flows through these six stages in roughly 50 milliseconds.
Solves cold-start for brand-new hotels while letting mature hotels specialise on their own data.
n = real booking outcomes · k = smoothing constant (20)

Competing chains share a market cluster — but never a single model weight or training row.

Nine discrete tiers. The bandit picks one; the price is the reference rate nudged by that offset.
Price = Reference Rate × (1 + arm offset) Reference Rate = BAR × Room × Rate-Plan × Length-of-Stay
Only prices a guest actually saw can teach the model. Rejected recommendations never train it.
Smarter decisions next time — confidence rises, fewer approvals needed
What the model sees before every single decision.
DEMAND occupancy · ADR trend · pace vs STLY · pickup 7d · inventory
COMP-SET avg rate · our index · rate trend · rank · dispersion
EVENTS event flag · intensity 0–1 (local concert → Super Bowl)
SEGMENT guest segment · room type · rate plan · length of stay
CALENDAR day of week · lead time to arrival
Three signals decide whether a price auto-publishes or waits for a human.
Sample size — how much real data does this hotel have?
Bag agreement — do the 5 members concur?
Decision margin — is the winner clearly ahead?
Three training rhythms, one automated quality gate. The model can never ship worse than yesterday.
